question_text: At DLA Piper, we believe great business can make a better world. We believe in being collaborative, bold, exceptional, and supportive. We are keen to hear what inspired your application. Why are you interested in starting a legal career at DLA Piper? (Max 200 words/1,500 Characters)
sample_answer: DLA Piper’s strong regional presence, expertise in employment law, and commendable pro bono work drew me to the firm. Having spoken to various trainees, such as Ahmed Syed, at the firm from different offices at Bright Network’s Future Lawyers event it was clear that through the firm’s One UK approach, DLA offers similar experiences and opportunities across all of its offices. This appeals to me as someone with a strong connection to the north who wants to build a career there. Additionally, DLA’s experience in employment law, with a tier one legal 500 ranking for Leeds and West Yorkshire is attractive to me as someone interested in this area. DLA’s work on the headline Uber case, advising the company on the outcome of the classification of its drivers as workers intrigued me and illustrated the calibre of work the firm is involved with. Therefore, my aspirations to conduct work of high commercial importance in the north drew me to the firm. On top of this, the firm’s work as a partner of the charity KIND UK providing advice to undocumented children aligns with my values and commitment to social justice, further attracting me to a legal career at DLA Piper.

question_text: If successful in securing a training contract after the Summer Internship, what do you anticipate will be the key challenges of the International Training Programme for you? How would you approach these challenges, and what resources or support do you believe you would need to overcome them? (Max 200 words/1,500 Characters)
sample_answer: I anticipate that there will be two key challenges of the International Training Programme, the first of which is time management. Engaging in challenging work such as high-profile cross-border transactions across the Programme will be very time-consuming, especially for trainees looking to develop their knowledge and skills in unfamiliar areas. I would approach this by prioritising tasks effectively, initially drawing upon advice from a supervisor to understand which tasks need to be completed as a priority and then considering this advice when completing work in the future. I would also communicate with fellow trainees to build a support network and ensure that we are all in this together. Secondly, another key challenge will be adjusting to different individuals both within and outside of the firm. Being exposed to four practice areas, potential secondment opportunities, and meeting various clients as part of the Training Programme will require versatility from trainees to adjust to these environments. To approach this I would continue to develop my communication and active listening skills to understand acceptable ways to communicate in these different environments and adjust accordingly. I would also make efforts to build positive working relationships with colleagues and clients alike.

How to manage demanding cross-border / unfamiliar work
How to adapt across multiple practice environments and stakeholders

Relationship-building is a core training-programme competency

question_text: At DLA Piper, we believe great business can make a better world. We believe in being bold, driven, compassionate, and collaborative. We are keen to hear what inspired your application. Why are you interested in starting a legal career at DLA Piper? (200 words/1,500 characters)
sample_answer: My application is inspired by DLA Piper's commitment to redefining what it means to be a truly global full-service law firm. Through work experience in the Sheffield office's litigation team, interactions with university alumni, trainees and associates, I have already experienced first-hand the firm's inclusive culture and the passion it's individuals have for the DLA brand. DLA Piper's dedication to fostering strong, supportive networks both internally and within the local community highlights its position as a market leader in terms of mindful business and social responsibility. The firm's impactful work in developing countries resonates with me deeply. Earlier this year, I travelled to Lesotho to address local human rights issues and collaborate with the charity Africa's Gift, to make eco-cook bags for the community. This experience ignited my passion to continue contributing to global initiatives, and I believe DLA offers the ideal platform to continue this work. Most importantly, DLA Piper's values are strongly aligned with my own; being supportive and collaborative within the community and with colleagues, being bold and exceptional in not only its work output, but in the relationships, individuals can build internally and externally is the driving quality of the firm.

How would you approach these challenges, and what resources or support do you believe you would need to overcome them? (200 words/1,500 characters)
sample_answer: If successful, I anticipate that one key challenge of the International Training Programme would be building a personal brand in an environment which fosters remote working across the UK. I am excited to take on this challenge and take advantage of DLA Piper’s opportunities to mould a brand personal to me. There are many opportunities for this support, but the most appealing is the firm’s commitment to its sectors providing a holistic and helpful approach to clients. Networks such as the NextGen CGFR and life sciences networks are amazing resources to network with juniors and share experiences and knowledge. DLA Piper’s ‘one UK’ approach excites me as a junior embarking on their career in law. Not only does this offer unparalleled opportunities to network across the UK, but also demonstrates cohesion on a global stage that has been incredible to experience during my work experience; I believe navigating life as a trainee and associate it all about taking every opportunity available and being a personal and approachable individual. I believe my ability to recognise and adapt to different working styles will benefit me personally and ensure I contribute effectively to DLA Piper’s collaborative, bold and accepting working environment.

question_text: Describe the personal event or experience that, more than anything else, made you realise your desire to work in a law firm and specifically at Fieldfisher. (800 characters)
sample_answer: ACCESS was a scheme run by Clifford Chance to help disadvantaged sixth formers break into commercial law. An application made in curiosity gave me the chance to argue before a part-time judge, and present an elevator pitch before three partners. These experiences were wholly unique to me at the time given the background I was from, and ignited my desire to work in a law firm. What made me realise I want to work at Fieldfisher is my current study of Intellectual Property law at university. I see the value in pursuing more niche practice to get engaged in more under-explored and thus cutting edge work. So Fieldfisher's Band 1 ranking in Clinical Negligence, and offering of services like Immigration and IP, sets the firm out from city competitors that have neglected these niches to me.
